items.title: Parcel locker notice
items.passage:
PARCEL LOCKERS
Collect your parcel within 48 hours of the arrival message. After that, it moves to the staffed counter, which opens at noon. A locker code will no longer work once the parcel has moved. Bring photo identification to the counter.

questions.stem: Where is a parcel collected after two days?

At the original locker
At the delivery depot
At the reception desk before noon
questions.evidence: After that, it moves to the staffed counter
questions.explanation: Evidence: “After that, it moves to the staffed counter” The location changes after 48 hours; the locker and depot are not the collection point.

questions.stem: Why might a valid arrival code stop working?
options: The collection period for the locker has ended
The counter has opened early
Photo identification has been submitted
The parcel has not yet arrived
questions.evidence: A locker code will no longer work once the parcel has moved
questions.explanation: Evidence: “A locker code will no longer work once the parcel has moved” Expiry changes the collection procedure; a working code is not restored by showing identification.

items.title: Museum evening entry
items.passage:

Gallery admission is free after 5 p.m.; the special exhibition still requires a ticket. Last entry to both is at 7:15. The café closes at 6, but visitors may remain in the galleries until 8.

options: The special exhibition
Entry to the galleries
Remaining until 8
Thursday café entry
questions.evidence: the special exhibition still requires a ticket
questions.explanation: Evidence: “the special exhibition still requires a ticket” Free admission applies to the galleries rather than every museum service.

questions.stem: Which visitor can still enter a gallery?
options: Someone arriving at 7:10
Someone arriving at 7:30
Someone arriving at 7:45
Someone arriving at 8:00
questions.evidence: Last entry to both is at 7:15
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Last entry to both is at 7:15” Closing time and last-entry time differ; being open until 8 does not permit later entry.

items.title: Shared refrigerator label
items.passage:
KITCHEN REMINDER
Label food with your name and the date you put it in the refrigerator. On Fridays at 4 p.m., cleaners remove unlabelled containers. Sealed drinks are exempt. A container's appearance does not tell the cleaners whether its owner intends to keep it.

questions.stem: Which item does NOT face Friday removal for a missing label?
options: A sealed drink
An unopened lunch box
A fresh-looking sandwich
A container with a name but no date
questions.evidence: Sealed drinks are exempt
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Sealed drinks are exempt” The exemption is specific to sealed drinks, not fresh food or any closed container.

questions.stem: Why mention the appearance of a container?
options: To explain why a label is necessary
To recommend transparent food boxes
To instruct cleaners to inspect the contents
To discourage bringing homemade meals
questions.evidence: A container's appearance does not tell the cleaners whether its owner intends to keep it
questions.explanation: Evidence: “A container's appearance does not tell the cleaners whether its owner intends to keep it” Appearance cannot communicate the owner’s intention; the point supports labelling.

items.title: Bus ticket transfer
items.passage:
CITY BUS TICKETS
Your ticket allows one transfer within 60 minutes of your first boarding. The transfer must continue your journey in the same direction. Return trips need a new ticket, even when they begin within the hour. Keep the original ticket for inspection.

questions.stem: Who needs to buy another ticket?
options: A passenger returning home 30 minutes later
A passenger continuing outward after 20 minutes
A passenger changing buses outward after 50 minutes
A passenger showing the original ticket on the next bus
questions.evidence: Return trips need a new ticket
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Return trips need a new ticket” The direction restriction applies even inside the 60-minute period.

questions.stem: When does the transfer period begin?
options: At the first boarding
When the ticket is inspected
When the passenger changes buses
When the outward journey ends
questions.evidence: within 60 minutes of your first boarding
questions.explanation: Evidence: “within 60 minutes of your first boarding” The clock starts on boarding, not on transfer or inspection.

items.title: Laundry machine message

The door remains locked for two minutes after the cycle ends. Please do not pull the handle during this interval. If the display shows ERROR rather than END, contact reception; restarting the machine can erase information the technician needs.

Wait for a new wash cycle
Pull the door firmly
Restart the machine
questions.evidence: contact reception

It keeps the door locked for a full day
It sends an unnecessary message to reception
questions.evidence: restarting the machine can erase information the technician needs
questions.explanation: Evidence: “restarting the machine can erase information the technician needs” The concern is preserving information for repair, not a stated fee or longer lock.

items.title: Clinic appointment reminder

Arrive ten minutes early to update your details. If you arrive more than fifteen minutes after your scheduled time, we may need to rebook you. Cancelling online frees your slot immediately; leaving a voicemail does not cancel it until staff confirm.

questions.evidence: Cancelling online frees your slot immediately

Verify the patient’s identity
Shorten the current consultation
Change the clinic’s records
questions.evidence: we may need to rebook you

items.title: Concert rehearsal access
items.passage:
REHEARSAL
Performers should enter through the stage door from 6 p.m. The auditorium opens to audience members at 7:15. Friends collecting performers after rehearsal may wait in the lobby but cannot enter backstage without a pass.

options: The stage door
The auditorium entrance
The lobby exit
The backstage entrance reserved for guests
questions.evidence: enter through the stage door from 6 p.m.
questions.explanation: Evidence: “enter through the stage door from 6 p.m.” Audience access begins later and is a different route.

questions.stem: What permission does a friend need to go backstage?
options: A backstage pass
A concert reservation
A performer’s pickup message
Arrival before 7:15
questions.evidence: cannot enter backstage without a pass
questions.explanation: Evidence: “cannot enter backstage without a pass” Waiting in the lobby or knowing a performer does not authorize backstage entry.

items.title: Digital assignment upload
items.passage:
UPLOAD HELP
The system records the time when an upload finishes, not when it begins. Large files may take several minutes. You can replace a submission until the deadline; the latest completed version is graded. Keep the confirmation email as proof of receipt.

questions.stem: Which version of an assignment is graded?

The first version selected for upload
The largest version in the upload queue
The version that began uploading last
questions.evidence: the latest completed version is graded
questions.explanation: Evidence: “the latest completed version is graded” Completion before the deadline matters; starting the upload is insufficient.

options: To encourage allowing time for upload completion
To prohibit assignments with illustrations
To offer an automatic deadline extension
To recommend uploading multiple versions together
questions.evidence: records the time when an upload finishes
questions.explanation: Evidence: “records the time when an upload finishes” The delay matters because only the finishing time is recorded.

items.title: Refill shop opening
items.passage:
REFILL SHOP
Bring a clean empty container. Staff weigh it before filling and subtract that weight when calculating your purchase. We lend containers for a refundable deposit if you forget yours. Containers returned with product still inside cannot be accepted for a refund.

questions.stem: Why is the empty container weighed?
options: To exclude its weight from the purchase charge
To determine whether it can be borrowed
To calculate the refundable deposit
To decide which product fits inside
questions.evidence: subtract that weight when calculating your purchase
questions.explanation: Evidence: “subtract that weight when calculating your purchase” Customers pay for the product’s weight rather than container weight.

questions.stem: How can a borrowed-container user receive the deposit back?
options: Return the container empty
Return it partly filled
Buy a different product
Ask staff to add its weight
questions.evidence: Containers returned with product still inside cannot be accepted for a refund
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Containers returned with product still inside cannot be accepted for a refund” Emptying the container is a required condition for return.

items.title: Borrowing sports shoes
items.passage:
SHOE LOANS
Indoor shoes are available for court users who have outdoor footwear only. Sizes are limited; advance reservations are not accepted. Borrowing is free, but users must leave an identification card until the shoes are returned. No shoes may leave the sports centre.

options: An identification card
A booking confirmation
A rental payment
Their outdoor shoes
questions.evidence: leave an identification card until the shoes are returned
questions.explanation: Evidence: “leave an identification card until the shoes are returned” The card secures the loan; borrowing has no fee.

questions.stem: What uncertainty remains for someone planning to borrow shoes?
options: Whether the right size will be available
Whether the loan requires payment
Whether shoes may be taken home
Whether advance booking guarantees a pair
questions.evidence: Sizes are limited; advance reservations are not accepted
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Sizes are limited; advance reservations are not accepted” The service is free, but availability cannot be reserved.

items.title: Language exchange board
items.passage:
LANGUAGE EXCHANGE
Post your preferred language and available meeting times. Contact details are visible only to registered members. This board introduces partners; it does not schedule meetings or provide tutors. Remove your post when you find a partner, so others see current requests.

questions.stem: What is the board’s main role?
options: Helping members find exchange partners
Assigning professional language tutors
Booking rooms for language classes
Arranging a weekly meeting timetable
questions.evidence: This board introduces partners
questions.explanation: Evidence: “This board introduces partners” It supports introductions while leaving scheduling to the users.

questions.stem: Who can view contact details?
options: Registered members
Every visitor to the website
Only the board’s tutors
Only someone already matched
questions.evidence: visible only to registered members
questions.explanation: Evidence: “visible only to registered members” Registration, rather than matching or tutor status, controls visibility.

items.title: Charity collection
items.passage:
DONATION DAY
Bring clean clothing to the hall between 9 and noon. We cannot accept electrical items at this collection. Books may be left in the marked box outside at any time, but clothing left there overnight can become damp and will not be collected.

questions.stem: Which donation follows the instructions?
options: Books in the marked box at 7 p.m.
Clothes in the outside box overnight
A lamp at the hall at 10 a.m.
Clothes at the hall after noon
questions.evidence: Books may be left in the marked box outside at any time
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Books may be left in the marked box outside at any time” Only books have unrestricted box access; the clothing and electrical-item rules differ.

questions.stem: Why should clothing not be left outside overnight?
options: It may become too damp to collect
The box is reserved for electrical items
All donations must be registered indoors
Staff collect it only after midnight
questions.evidence: can become damp and will not be collected
questions.explanation: Evidence: “can become damp and will not be collected” The stated reason concerns condition, not registration or night staffing.

items.title: Café reusable cup offer
items.passage:
REUSABLE CUP OFFER
Receive a discount on takeaway coffee when you bring your own cup. The cup must be clean and large enough for your chosen drink. The discount does not apply to drinks consumed in the café, where washable cups are already provided.

questions.stem: Which customer qualifies for the discount?
options: Someone taking coffee away in a suitable clean cup
Someone drinking inside with a personal cup
Someone borrowing a takeaway cup from staff
Someone bringing a cup too small for the order
questions.evidence: on takeaway coffee when you bring your own cup
questions.explanation: Evidence: “on takeaway coffee when you bring your own cup” Takeaway use and a suitable personal cup are both required.

questions.stem: Why mention the café’s washable cups?
options: To explain the exclusion of drinks consumed inside
To ask customers to wash cups for staff
To advertise a new takeaway cup size
To extend the discount to seated customers
questions.evidence: where washable cups are already provided
questions.explanation: Evidence: “where washable cups are already provided” Inside service already uses reusable cups, explaining the offer’s scope.

items.title: Campus bike repairs
items.passage:
BIKE REPAIR DROP-IN
Mechanics assess faults for free. Replacement parts are charged separately, and no repair begins until you approve the cost. Minor adjustments may be completed while you wait. For larger repairs, staff will arrange a collection time after the assessment.

questions.stem: What must happen before a paid repair starts?
options: The owner approves the cost
The owner buys a replacement bike
Staff set the drop-in closing time
The free assessment is skipped
questions.evidence: no repair begins until you approve the cost
questions.explanation: Evidence: “no repair begins until you approve the cost” Assessment does not automatically authorize paid work.

questions.stem: Why might a bike need to stay at the workshop?
options: Its repair is too substantial for a while-you-wait service
The assessment itself always takes several days
Free repairs are handled only after paid ones
The owner has declined the proposed cost
questions.evidence: For larger repairs, staff will arrange a collection time
questions.explanation: Evidence: “For larger repairs, staff will arrange a collection time” Repair size affects timing; the other policies are not stated.

items.title: Repair café update
items.passage:
From: Community Workshop
Subject: Saturday repair café
We have received more requests for lamp repairs than expected, so an electrician will join us this Saturday. Please describe the fault on the booking form; bringing an item without a description makes it harder to assign the right volunteer. We cannot promise that every object can be repaired, and replacement parts are not included.
The morning session is fully booked. There are still afternoon appointments, but these are for small electrical items only. People bringing furniture should keep their existing morning appointments. If you booked a morning electrical repair and can move to the afternoon, please reply by Thursday. This would free a place for someone on the furniture waiting list.

questions.stem: Why is the workshop asking some morning customers to move?
options: To make room for furniture repairs
To give the electrician a shorter shift
To eliminate the furniture waiting list permanently
To replace all morning appointments
questions.evidence: This would free a place for someone on the furniture waiting list
questions.explanation: Evidence: “This would free a place for someone on the furniture waiting list” Only customers able to move are asked; furniture must remain in the morning.

questions.stem: Who can book a remaining afternoon appointment?
options: Someone with a small electrical item
Someone with a broken chair
Anyone already on the furniture waiting list
Anyone bringing an item without describing it
questions.evidence: these are for small electrical items only

questions.stem: What should a customer understand about replacement parts?

They are supplied free with every repair
They guarantee that an object can be fixed
They must be listed on the furniture waiting list

questions.explanation: Evidence: “replacement parts are not included” The service does not cover parts; the passage also declines to guarantee a repair.

items.title: Apartment heating inspection
items.passage:
Dear residents,
Engineers will inspect the building's heating system on Tuesday between 9 and 4. They need access to the radiator valves in each apartment, not to cupboards or storage rooms. Please move furniture that blocks a valve. Heating may stop briefly during the work, but hot water will remain available.
If nobody will be home, you can authorize the caretaker to admit the engineers. Submit the permission form by Monday noon; an email saying you will be away is not sufficient authorization. Residents who cannot provide access on Tuesday should contact the office for a separate appointment. Those visits will occur later in the week and will not include the shared-system checks carried out on Tuesday.

questions.stem: What must be accessible inside apartments?
options: The radiator valves
Every storage cupboard
The hot-water tank
All bedroom furniture
questions.evidence: They need access to the radiator valves
questions.explanation: Evidence: “They need access to the radiator valves” The required preparation is clearing the valves, not opening storage areas.

questions.stem: Which absent resident has authorized entry?
options: One who submits the permission form on time
One who emails that they are away
One who moves furniture without filing the form
One who requests a later appointment
questions.evidence: an email saying you will be away is not sufficient authorization
questions.explanation: Evidence: “an email saying you will be away is not sufficient authorization” Only the specified form authorizes the caretaker to admit engineers.

questions.stem: Which service is expected to remain available during Tuesday’s work?
options: Hot water
Uninterrupted heating
Separate apartment appointments
Access to shared-system checks later in the week
questions.evidence: hot water will remain available
questions.explanation: Evidence: “hot water will remain available” Heating can pause, while the shared checks are scheduled for Tuesday.

items.title: Newspaper correction
items.passage:
CORRECTION: Riverside redevelopment
Our Monday report stated that the riverside footpath would close throughout the redevelopment. The council has now clarified that closure applies only to the eastern section beside the old warehouse. The western section will remain open, although cyclists will be asked to dismount near the temporary work entrance.
The article also described the planned café as council-operated. The building belongs to the council, but a local cooperative will run the café under a lease. Opening is expected in spring, subject to the completion of safety inspections. We regret the errors. The online article has been updated, while copies of the original printed newspaper cannot be altered. A summary of the correction will appear in tomorrow's print edition.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of this text?
options: To correct two claims in an earlier report
To announce the cancellation of redevelopment
To invite applications to operate a café
To compare two newspapers’ coverage
questions.evidence: We regret the errors
questions.explanation: Evidence: “We regret the errors” It corrects the path-closure scope and the café’s operator.

questions.stem: Who will operate the café?
options: A local cooperative
The council’s parks department
The old warehouse owner
The newspaper’s publisher
questions.evidence: a local cooperative will run the café under a lease
questions.explanation: Evidence: “a local cooperative will run the café under a lease” Building ownership is distinct from day-to-day operation.

questions.stem: Why might spring opening be delayed?
options: Safety inspections may not be completed in time
The western path has to close first
The printed correction must be withdrawn
Cyclists are unwilling to dismount
questions.evidence: subject to the completion of safety inspections
questions.explanation: Evidence: “subject to the completion of safety inspections” The projected opening is conditional, not a firm guarantee.

items.title: Accessible tour arrangements
items.passage:
To: Visitors booked on the heritage tour
The guided route normally includes a staircase to the upper gallery. Anyone who prefers to avoid stairs can join the same guide in the ground-floor study room for the final part of the tour. There, digital images show the objects displayed upstairs, and replicas of two items can be handled. This alternative takes the same amount of time as the gallery visit.
Please tell us your preferred route when confirming your booking. There is no additional charge, and you do not need to explain your reason for choosing the study room. The lift reaches the first floor but not the upper gallery. Staff at reception can answer questions about access before the tour begins; arriving early will give them more time to help.

questions.stem: What can visitors do in the study room?
options: Handle replicas of two objects
Use the lift to the upper gallery
View every original object upstairs
Complete the whole tour without a guide
questions.evidence: replicas of two items can be handled
questions.explanation: Evidence: “replicas of two items can be handled” The study room provides images and replicas, not the upper-gallery originals.

questions.stem: What is true of choosing the alternative route?

It requires proof that stairs cannot be used
It ends earlier than the usual visit
It incurs an extra charge
questions.evidence: you do not need to explain your reason
questions.explanation: Evidence: “you do not need to explain your reason” The choice is available without justification, extra payment, or shorter duration.

To suggest that reception should move upstairs
To announce that the lift is being repaired
To require visitors to use the staircase
questions.evidence: not the upper gallery
questions.explanation: Evidence: “not the upper gallery” A lift exists but does not solve access to that particular destination.

items.title: Research participation invitation
items.passage:
The university transport team is seeking volunteers to keep a travel diary for one week. We want to understand journeys that do not appear in bus-ticket records, including walking, cycling, and trips that people considered but did not make. You do not need to use public transport to participate.
The diary asks for approximate starting areas rather than full addresses. Please avoid identifying other passengers or recording conversations. At the end of the week, participants can attend an optional discussion about the findings. The thank-you voucher is provided when the diary is submitted, whether or not you attend that discussion. Applications close Friday, but the diary week begins the following Monday. We cannot accept a diary that was completed before registration.

questions.stem: Why collect information about walking and abandoned trips?
options: These are missing from ticket records
They require more expensive bus tickets
They identify individual passengers
They replace the need for participant registration
questions.evidence: journeys that do not appear in bus-ticket records
questions.explanation: Evidence: “journeys that do not appear in bus-ticket records” The diary complements existing data with otherwise invisible travel decisions.

questions.stem: What is required to receive a voucher?
options: Submitting the diary
Attending the discussion
Providing a full home address
Travelling by bus daily
questions.evidence: provided when the diary is submitted
questions.explanation: Evidence: “provided when the diary is submitted” Discussion attendance and public transport use are not conditions.

questions.stem: Which diary would be ineligible?
options: One completed before the writer registered
One including journeys on foot
One using approximate starting areas
One from someone who skips the discussion
questions.evidence: We cannot accept a diary that was completed before registration
questions.explanation: Evidence: “We cannot accept a diary that was completed before registration” The study requires registration before the diary period.

items.title: Restaurant group reservation
items.passage:
Thank you for reserving a table for twelve on Sunday. For groups of ten or more, we ask you to choose either the set menu or a shared buffet in advance. The buffet includes vegetarian dishes; the set menu has a vegetarian main course available on request. Please send any allergy information separately so the kitchen can assess it. Choosing a vegetarian dish alone does not tell us about allergies.
We hold tables for fifteen minutes after the booked time. If your group is delayed, call us rather than replying to this email, which may not be checked during service. Your deposit will be deducted from the final bill. It becomes nonrefundable after Friday, even if fewer guests attend. We can adjust food quantities until Saturday noon.

questions.stem: How should a delayed group contact the restaurant?
options: By telephone
By replying to this email
Through the kitchen’s allergy form
By changing the deposit payment
questions.evidence: call us rather than replying to this email
questions.explanation: Evidence: “call us rather than replying to this email” Email may go unread during service, so a call is required.

questions.stem: Why send allergy details separately from a menu choice?
options: A vegetarian choice does not specify allergy risks
The buffet contains no vegetarian dishes
All menu choices automatically exclude allergens
Only set-menu guests can report allergies
questions.evidence: Choosing a vegetarian dish alone does not tell us about allergies
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Choosing a vegetarian dish alone does not tell us about allergies” Dietary preference and allergy information serve different purposes.

options: It is subtracted from the final bill
It is refunded separately before Friday
It is added as a service charge
It pays only for guests who do not attend

questions.explanation: Evidence: “deducted from the final bill” The deposit is an advance payment, not an additional charge.

items.title: Second-hand laptop listing
items.passage:
FOR SALE: student laptop
I am selling my laptop because my new course requires specialist graphics software. The machine still runs ordinary office programs well. Its battery lasts about two hours, so I usually keep it plugged in during long classes. A charger is included, but the protective case shown in the photograph is not.
You are welcome to test the laptop in the library café before buying. I have reset it, so no course software remains installed. Please do not expect technical support after the sale; I am a student, not a repair business. I will consider sensible offers, but I cannot exchange it for another device. Collection is available this weekend. I can reserve it only after we agree on a collection time.

options: Someone needing basic office programs with access to power
Someone expecting specialist graphics software preinstalled
Someone needing all-day unplugged use
Someone seeking continuing repair support

The charger
The reset laptop
The opportunity to test it
questions.evidence: the protective case shown in the photograph is not

Suggestions for other devices to exchange
Requests for technical advice
Offers to reserve without a pickup plan

questions.explanation: Evidence: “I will consider sensible offers” The seller is open to realistic price negotiation, but rules out exchanges.

items.title: Community choir welcome
items.passage:
Welcome to the neighbourhood choir. There is no audition, and reading music is not a requirement. At the first rehearsal, the conductor will listen to singers in small groups to suggest a comfortable vocal part. This is placement, not a selection process; everyone who has registered has a place.
Rehearsals are on Wednesdays. We record each part separately so members can practise at home, but the recordings do not replace attendance. Please contact the conductor if you will miss several rehearsals. Performances are optional, though anyone choosing to perform must attend the final rehearsal. The membership fee covers room hire and sheet music. Concert clothing is arranged separately, and we try to use items members already own to avoid unnecessary purchases.

questions.stem: Why does the message distinguish placement from selection?
options: To reassure members that listening does not determine admission
To explain why an audition is compulsory
To encourage singers to change choirs
To remove singers who cannot read music
questions.evidence: everyone who has registered has a place
questions.explanation: Evidence: “everyone who has registered has a place” The conductor’s listening assigns a part rather than deciding membership.

questions.stem: Who must attend the final rehearsal?
options: Members who choose to perform
Every person who has downloaded recordings
Only members who read music
Only singers with new concert clothing
questions.evidence: anyone choosing to perform must attend the final rehearsal
questions.explanation: Evidence: “anyone choosing to perform must attend the final rehearsal” Performance is optional, but preparation for it has a condition.

questions.stem: What is the intended use of the recordings?
options: Supplementing rehearsals with practice at home
Replacing Wednesday attendance entirely
Auditioning new members remotely
Providing clothing instructions
questions.evidence: the recordings do not replace attendance
questions.explanation: Evidence: “the recordings do not replace attendance” Home recordings support practice rather than substitute for group rehearsal.

items.title: Refund request response
items.passage:
Dear customer,
We have reviewed your request concerning the damaged bookshelf. The photographs show that one side panel arrived cracked, and we can send a replacement panel at no cost. This does not require you to return the whole unit. If you prefer a full refund, however, the complete bookshelf must be collected by our carrier.
Please retain the packaging until you decide which option you want. The carrier needs the item packed securely, although it does not have to be dismantled if it fits safely in the original box. We can arrange collection on a weekday, but cannot guarantee a precise time until the carrier confirms its route. Let us know your choice within fourteen days of this message. That deadline applies to requesting a remedy, not to completing the collection.

questions.stem: What must be returned for a full refund?
options: The complete bookshelf
Only the cracked panel
Only the original packaging
The photographs of the damage
questions.evidence: the complete bookshelf must be collected

options: The customer must communicate the preferred remedy
The carrier must finish collecting the item
The customer must assemble the replacement panel
The carrier must guarantee a pickup hour
questions.evidence: requesting a remedy, not to completing the collection
questions.explanation: Evidence: “requesting a remedy, not to completing the collection” The deadline governs the request, not carrier timing.

questions.stem: Why is the customer asked to keep the packaging?

It is needed to verify the photographs
It must be returned for a panel replacement
It determines the refund amount
questions.evidence: The carrier needs the item packed securely
questions.explanation: Evidence: “The carrier needs the item packed securely” Packaging supports safe transport if the refund option is chosen.

items.title: Cooking class equipment
items.passage:
Our bread-making class is suitable for beginners. Ingredients and mixing bowls are supplied, but please bring an apron and a container for taking your loaf home. The class uses wheat flour, and we cannot offer a gluten-free version in the same kitchen. Participants who cannot handle wheat should contact us before booking rather than assume a substitute can be arranged.
You will mix and shape a small loaf, then watch the instructor demonstrate a longer fermentation method. Because that method takes several hours, the demonstration dough will have been prepared earlier. Your own loaf will use a shorter process so it can be baked during the class. We will explain the difference and provide both recipes. Arrive ten minutes early; the shared oven schedule makes it difficult to accommodate late starts.

questions.stem: What should participants bring?
options: An apron and a takeaway container
Wheat flour and a mixing bowl
Prepared demonstration dough
A private oven tray and all ingredients
questions.evidence: bring an apron and a container

Beginners are not allowed to mix dough
The shared oven cannot bake demonstration loaves
The class is exclusively about gluten-free recipes
questions.evidence: that method takes several hours

To warn that the instructor’s recipe is unreliable
To exclude beginners from fermentation practice
To suggest that only one recipe will be provided

questions.explanation: Evidence: “Your own loaf will use a shorter process” Timing accounts for the difference; both recipes remain available.

items.title: Festival volunteer shifts
items.passage:
Festival volunteers,
Please check the revised rota before Saturday. Some afternoon information-desk shifts have moved to the gate because advance ticket sales have reduced the number of questions expected at the desk. People assigned to equipment transport should report to the loading area, not the gate. A blue badge identifies that team, while all other volunteers wear green badges. Badges are for identification and do not authorize entry to every area. In particular, performers' rooms remain restricted to those assigned there. Lunch vouchers can be collected after your first shift; volunteers working only in the evening can collect theirs on arrival. Please tell the coordinator about any clash with your availability by Wednesday.

Ticket scanners require blue badges

Only after collecting a lunch voucher

The information desk
The main gate
The performers’ rooms

items.title: Book club format change
items.passage:

The library has put copies on reserve. These must be read in the building so all members have access, but an authorized digital edition is available through the catalogue. Please do not circulate photographs of the reserve copies. We will meet in the usual room at 6, with an online connection for members who are away. To replace all future novels with digital texts
To require every member to attend online

items.title: Rainwater tank notice
items.passage:

To reduce congestion, fill watering cans at the tank and carry them to your plot rather than attaching long hoses. A hose may be used for the communal beds by the person assigned to that week's maintenance shift. This exception does not extend to individual plots. We will record usage for the first month to see whether the tank meets demand. If it does not, the committee will consider another tank, but no additional purchase has been approved.

options: The maintenance volunteer watering communal beds
Any plot holder using it before others arrive
Anyone whose individual plot is far away
Only committee members deciding on another tank
questions.evidence: for the communal beds by the person assigned

It has been ordered for next month
It is required before the first tank opens
It will replace the mains backup immediately
questions.evidence: no additional purchase has been approved

To prevent staff from measuring water use

questions.explanation: Evidence: “To reduce congestion” The rule manages access, not water treatment or measurement.

items.title: Local history archive access
items.passage:
The town archive now offers appointments to consult family records. When booking, give the approximate dates and names you are researching so staff can identify relevant boxes beforehand. An appointment reserves a workspace, not a promise that the archive holds the information you need. Some records were lost before the collection was established.
Pencils and laptops are permitted at the desk; pens and food are not. You may photograph unrestricted documents for personal research without flash, but staff must check each file for privacy restrictions first. A document's age alone does not establish permission. If you want to publish an image, request written approval separately. Staff can help locate sources, but they cannot conduct a full family-history investigation during your visit. Appointments are limited to ninety minutes when other readers are waiting.

questions.stem: Why should a researcher provide names and dates beforehand?
options: To help staff prepare relevant material
To guarantee that every requested record exists
To obtain publication permission automatically
To extend an appointment beyond ninety minutes
questions.evidence: identify relevant boxes beforehand
questions.explanation: Evidence: “identify relevant boxes beforehand” Advance information helps preparation without guaranteeing a discovery.

questions.stem: What is required before photographing a file?
options: A staff check for privacy restrictions
Proof that it is over a certain age
An appointment longer than ninety minutes
An application for a complete investigation
questions.evidence: staff must check each file for privacy restrictions first
questions.explanation: Evidence: “staff must check each file for privacy restrictions first” Age alone does not establish access permission.

questions.stem: What does “unrestricted” mean in this context?
options: Not subject to limits on access
Too old to be useful
Already researched by staff
Available for any commercial publication
questions.evidence: unrestricted documents for personal research
questions.explanation: Evidence: “unrestricted documents for personal research” Personal access does not automatically authorize publication.

items.title: Delivery route change
items.passage:
Dear subscription customers,
From next week, our vegetable-box deliveries will use one fixed day for each neighbourhood. This reduces repeated driving and should make arrival times more consistent. Your neighbourhood's day is Wednesday. You may request a different delivery address, but that address will follow its own neighbourhood schedule.
We cannot offer an individual choice of weekday. If Wednesday does not suit you, collect your box from the community shop after 4 p.m. on Tuesday instead. Shop collection must be selected by Sunday evening so we know how many boxes to leave there. Uncollected shop boxes are not automatically delivered the next day. We will hold them until Thursday closing time. The produce varies seasonally; changing the collection method does not change the contents or the subscription price.

questions.stem: What is the alternative to Wednesday delivery?
options: Tuesday shop collection after 4
Thursday delivery on request
Tuesday delivery before 4
Wednesday shop collection without notice
questions.evidence: collect your box from the community shop after 4 p.m. on Tuesday
questions.explanation: Evidence: “collect your box from the community shop after 4 p.m. on Tuesday” The alternative is collection on a specified earlier day.

questions.stem: How does using a different address affect delivery?
options: The new neighbourhood determines the day
The customer can choose any weekday
The original Wednesday schedule always follows the customer
The subscription price automatically rises
questions.evidence: that address will follow its own neighbourhood schedule
questions.explanation: Evidence: “that address will follow its own neighbourhood schedule” Schedules attach to areas rather than to an individual subscriber.

questions.stem: Which feature remains the same when shop collection is chosen?
options: The box contents and price
The deadline for choosing a collection method
The date the box becomes available
The automatic delivery of uncollected boxes
questions.evidence: does not change the contents or the subscription price
questions.explanation: Evidence: “does not change the contents or the subscription price” Collection changes logistics, not the produce allocation or charge.

items.title: Internship interview arrangements
items.passage:
Thank you for applying for the museum internship. Shortlisted applicants will have a twenty-minute interview and a brief task involving a sample visitor enquiry. The task checks how you organize information, not whether you already know the museum's collection. All necessary facts will be supplied.
Please choose an interview time through the booking link by Friday. Interviews can take place online or at the museum; neither option affects selection. If you need adjustments to participate, contact the recruitment team rather than the general ticket office. We will confirm arrangements privately. Applicants are welcome to visit the public galleries beforehand, but this is optional and paid admission will not be reimbursed. The internship begins in July; the interview invitation does not constitute an offer of a position.

questions.stem: What skill is the sample task designed to assess?
options: Organizing supplied information
Recalling collection facts from memory
Selling museum admission tickets
Choosing an online meeting platform
questions.evidence: checks how you organize information
questions.explanation: Evidence: “checks how you organize information” The museum supplies facts; prior collection knowledge is not the target.

questions.stem: Should an applicant visit the galleries to qualify?
options: No, a visit is optional
Yes, only visitors are shortlisted
Yes, and the admission fee will be refunded
No, applicants are prohibited from visiting
questions.evidence: this is optional and paid admission will not be reimbursed
questions.explanation: Evidence: “this is optional and paid admission will not be reimbursed” A visit is allowed but neither required nor funded.

questions.stem: Who handles participation adjustments?
options: The recruitment team
The general ticket office
The visitor enquiry desk
The gallery admission staff
questions.evidence: contact the recruitment team
questions.explanation: Evidence: “contact the recruitment team” The message explicitly routes these requests away from ticketing.

items.title: Shared study subscription
items.passage:
Our study-space membership now includes five guest visits per term. Each visit admits one guest for one day; bringing two guests on the same day uses two visits. A member must accompany guests and remain in the building while they use the space. Guest visits cannot be transferred to another member's account.
Weekend access for members continues as before, but guests are admitted only when reception is staffed, from Monday to Friday. Meeting-room reservations are charged separately, even if all participants are members. Quiet booths are available without booking on a first-come basis. We have added this distinction to the price page because several members assumed that every room was included. Existing members will receive the guest allowance automatically at the start of the next term; no new application is required.

questions.stem: How many allowance visits does bringing two guests for one day use?
options: Two
One
Five
None
questions.evidence: bringing two guests on the same day uses two visits
questions.explanation: Evidence: “bringing two guests on the same day uses two visits” The allowance counts guest-days, not occasions on which a member brings someone.

questions.stem: Can a member bring a guest on Saturday?
options: No, guest entry is limited to staffed weekdays
Yes, because member weekend access is unchanged
Yes, if only one guest visit is used
Only if a quiet booth is reserved
questions.evidence: guests are admitted only when reception is staffed, from Monday to Friday
questions.explanation: Evidence: “guests are admitted only when reception is staffed, from Monday to Friday” Member access and guest access have different conditions.

questions.stem: Why was the room-price distinction added online?
options: To correct an assumption about included facilities
To remove all quiet booths from membership
To require existing members to reapply
To allow guest visits to be transferred
questions.evidence: several members assumed that every room was included
questions.explanation: Evidence: “several members assumed that every room was included” The clarification distinguishes free booths from paid meeting-room reservations.

items.title: Neighbourhood survey results
items.passage:
Thank you to everyone who completed the square-redesign survey. Most respondents favoured more seating, while opinions about a new fountain were divided. These results will guide the design team, but the survey was not a vote authorizing construction. Costs and access requirements still need review.
The online form attracted many responses from people who pass through the square on their way to work. Fewer nearby residents responded than we had hoped. We will therefore hold two drop-in sessions at the community centre to hear from residents who did not use the form. This does not invalidate the responses already received. It helps us avoid designing solely around the views of the easiest group to reach. A draft plan will be displayed next month, before any final decision is made.

questions.stem: What can be concluded about the seating proposal?
options: It has support among survey respondents but is not yet approved
It was authorized by a binding public vote
It will be built before cost review
It received unanimous support from nearby residents
questions.evidence: the survey was not a vote authorizing construction
questions.explanation: Evidence: “the survey was not a vote authorizing construction” Survey support informs design while further decisions remain.

questions.stem: Why are drop-in sessions planned?
options: To include residents underrepresented in the online responses
To discard opinions from commuters
To count votes for the already approved fountain
To replace the design team with volunteers
questions.evidence: Fewer nearby residents responded than we had hoped
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Fewer nearby residents responded than we had hoped” The sessions broaden participation rather than erase the earlier data.

questions.stem: What does “invalidate” mean here?
options: Make something no longer usable or acceptable
Make something easier to display
Make something more expensive
Make something public for the first time
questions.evidence: This does not invalidate the responses already received
questions.explanation: Evidence: “This does not invalidate the responses already received” Additional outreach does not make previous responses worthless.

items.title: Lost-property procedure
items.passage:
If you have lost something at the theatre, submit a description using our online form. Include the date, approximate seat location, and distinguishing features. Do not include bank-card numbers or other sensitive information. Staff compare your description with the items received; a general claim such as 'a black bag' may not be sufficient.
We cannot search the auditorium while a performance is taking place. Items found after a show are logged the following morning. Please wait for confirmation before travelling to collect anything. A matching description is necessary, but staff may also ask you to show identification. If a friend collects an item for you, authorize that person by replying to our confirmation message. Unclaimed items are held for thirty days, except perishable food, which is discarded at the end of the day.

questions.stem: When are items found after a show entered into the records?
options: The following morning
During that performance
Only when an owner arrives
Thirty days after discovery
questions.evidence: logged the following morning
questions.explanation: Evidence: “logged the following morning” Logging follows the show, so an immediate online search may be incomplete.

questions.stem: What should an owner do before sending a friend to collect an item?
options: Reply to the confirmation authorizing that friend
Give the friend a bank-card number
Submit another vague claim under the friend’s name
Wait until the thirty-day holding period ends
questions.evidence: authorize that person by replying to our confirmation message
questions.explanation: Evidence: “authorize that person by replying to our confirmation message” The collector needs authorization, not merely knowledge of the loss.

questions.stem: Why ask for distinguishing features?
options: To match the claim reliably to a particular item
To advertise unclaimed bags online
To avoid asking for the performance date
To permit searches during a show
questions.evidence: a general claim such as 'a black bag' may not be sufficient
questions.explanation: Evidence: “a general claim such as 'a black bag' may not be sufficient” Specific features improve identification where many items look similar.

items.title: Professional course credit
items.passage:
The weekend communication course is open to anyone interested in improving presentations. Employees who want the course to count toward their professional-development requirement must obtain their manager's approval before enrolment. Approval after attendance cannot be applied retrospectively. Other participants do not need an employer's permission.
The fee includes teaching materials and lunch, but not travel. Attendance at both days is required for a completion certificate. A participant who misses a day may join the next course for that day's sessions, subject to space, instead of repeating the whole weekend. This arrangement does not guarantee an immediate certificate. Please let the office know about an absence promptly so staff can advise on the available dates. The course certificate records completion; it does not certify that an employer has awarded development credit.

questions.stem: What must an employee do to seek development credit?
options: Get approval before enrolling
Present the certificate after any single day
Request approval only after attendance
Ask the course office to authorize employer credit
questions.evidence: must obtain their manager's approval before enrolment
questions.explanation: Evidence: “must obtain their manager's approval before enrolment” The employer controls credit approval and the timing is explicit.

questions.stem: What option is available after missing one day?
options: Attend the relevant day of a later course if space allows
Receive the certificate immediately
Repeat both days without checking capacity
Claim development credit retrospectively
questions.evidence: subject to space, instead of repeating the whole weekend
questions.explanation: Evidence: “subject to space, instead of repeating the whole weekend” A make-up day is possible but conditional.

questions.stem: What does “This arrangement” refer to?
options: Making up a missed day on the next course
Including lunch in the fee
Requesting a manager’s advance approval
Opening the course to the general public
questions.evidence: may join the next course for that day's sessions
questions.explanation: Evidence: “may join the next course for that day's sessions” The phrase refers to the make-up provision immediately before it.

items.title: Residents’ bicycle storage
items.passage:
From next month, indoor bicycle spaces will be allocated annually. Current users must renew their applications; having a space this year does not automatically reserve it next year. We will prioritize residents without access to private storage, then use a lottery if eligible applications exceed the available spaces.
A space permits storage of one bicycle, not repair work or charging of batteries. These restrictions reflect the room's ventilation and insurance conditions. Outdoor racks remain available without application. Please remove any bicycle you no longer use, since abandoned bicycles take capacity away from other residents. Staff will attach a notice to apparently abandoned bicycles before arranging removal. A bicycle is not considered abandoned simply because it is old. We will contact the registered user and allow fourteen days for a reply before taking further action.

questions.stem: Who receives priority for indoor spaces?
options: Residents without private storage
Residents with the newest bicycles
Everyone who used a space last year
Residents offering to repair other bicycles
questions.evidence: prioritize residents without access to private storage
questions.explanation: Evidence: “prioritize residents without access to private storage” Priority relates to storage need rather than prior use or bike value.

questions.stem: What happens when qualifying demand exceeds capacity?
options: A lottery selects among eligible applications
Every old bicycle is immediately removed
Current users automatically keep all spaces
Outdoor racks become application-only
questions.evidence: use a lottery if eligible applications exceed the available spaces
questions.explanation: Evidence: “use a lottery if eligible applications exceed the available spaces” The lottery resolves oversubscription after eligibility and priority.

questions.stem: Why mention that an old bicycle is not automatically abandoned?
options: To clarify that age alone does not justify removal
To exclude old bicycles from the lottery
To encourage charging older batteries indoors
To cancel contact with registered users
questions.evidence: not considered abandoned simply because it is old
questions.explanation: Evidence: “not considered abandoned simply because it is old” The notice distinguishes an appearance from evidence of abandonment.

items.title: Language course placement
items.passage:
Before the first class, please complete the short placement exercise. It helps us group learners with similar current skills. There is no passing mark, and using a dictionary or getting help would make the grouping less useful. If you have never studied the language, select the beginner option rather than completing the exercise.
Your initial group is provisional. Teachers may suggest a move after observing classroom work, and you can discuss your own concerns with them. A move depends on available space and may not happen immediately. The two evening groups use the same textbook but progress at different speeds. Buying the textbook before placement is therefore safe, although you should wait before purchasing the optional workbook, which differs by group. Refund requests are handled by the office under the standard enrolment terms, not by individual teachers.

questions.stem: Why should learners avoid help on the exercise?
options: Help could distort the estimate of their current skills
The exercise is a graded final examination
Dictionaries are forbidden throughout the course
Help would change the textbook price
questions.evidence: would make the grouping less useful
questions.explanation: Evidence: “would make the grouping less useful” The exercise is for placement, so independent performance is informative.

questions.stem: What can a learner safely purchase before placement?
options: The shared textbook
The group-specific workbook
A guaranteed transfer to another group
A refund approved by a teacher
questions.evidence: the same textbook but progress at different speeds
questions.explanation: Evidence: “the same textbook but progress at different speeds” Textbook choice does not depend on placement, unlike the workbook.

questions.stem: What does “provisional” mean here?
options: Subject to later adjustment
Determined by a passing mark
Reserved exclusively for beginners
Cancelled until materials are bought
questions.evidence: Teachers may suggest a move after observing classroom work
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Teachers may suggest a move after observing classroom work” The initial grouping can change as teachers gain more information.

items.title: Reusable packaging trial
items.passage:
Our bakery is testing returnable cake boxes for three months. Pay a deposit when collecting a box and receive it back when the empty box is returned undamaged. You may return it to either of our branches, regardless of where you bought the cake. Please remove leftover food, but do not put the box through a dishwasher; we clean returns using our own approved process.
The trial includes large celebration cakes only. Small cakes and pastries continue to use ordinary packaging. We will measure return rates and staff time before deciding whether to expand the scheme. A high return rate alone may not make it practical if processing requires too much labour. Your receipt separates the box deposit from the cake price, so please keep it until your deposit has been refunded.

questions.stem: Where may a box be returned?
options: Either branch
Only the branch of purchase
Only the central bakery
Any shop displaying ordinary packaging
questions.evidence: either of our branches
questions.explanation: Evidence: “either of our branches” The return location is flexible within the bakery’s own branches.

questions.stem: Why could the scheme fail despite many returned boxes?
options: Processing returns may demand too much staff time
Customers may choose the wrong cake flavour
Large cakes are excluded from the trial
Refunds are restricted to the original branch
questions.evidence: if processing requires too much labour
questions.explanation: Evidence: “if processing requires too much labour” Both return rate and operational burden inform expansion.

questions.stem: Which action should customers avoid?
options: Cleaning the box in a dishwasher
Removing leftover food
Keeping the receipt
Returning an undamaged box
questions.evidence: do not put the box through a dishwasher
questions.explanation: Evidence: “do not put the box through a dishwasher” Customers empty boxes; the bakery performs the approved cleaning.

items.title: Public lecture recording
items.passage:
Thank you for attending the astronomy lecture. A recording of the presentation will be posted on the library website next week. The audience discussion will not be included because some participants asked questions involving personal information. We will instead publish a written summary of the general scientific points raised.
The slides are available now, but some contain diagrams that make sense only alongside the speaker's explanation. Please do not interpret a diagram on its own as a recommendation or a complete account. The speaker has provided further-reading links for anyone who wants more detail. These resources are optional and include material at several levels. If you share the recording, use the library's link rather than uploading a separate copy, so viewers receive corrections if the page is updated. The original lecture date will remain visible beside the recording.

questions.stem: Why is the audience discussion excluded from the recording?
options: To avoid publishing personal information
To reduce the length of every slide
To prevent viewers from studying science
To remove the lecture date
questions.evidence: questions involving personal information
questions.explanation: Evidence: “questions involving personal information” A general written summary preserves scientific points while omitting the discussion audio.

questions.stem: What advantage does sharing the library’s link provide?
options: Viewers can receive later corrections
It guarantees every optional resource is introductory
It removes the need for the speaker’s explanation
It makes the audience discussion public
questions.evidence: so viewers receive corrections if the page is updated
questions.explanation: Evidence: “so viewers receive corrections if the page is updated” The library page remains the maintained version.

options: The presentation slides
The full audience recording
The corrected version of every resource
The presentation video scheduled for next week
questions.evidence: The slides are available now
questions.explanation: Evidence: “The slides are available now” The presentation recording is forthcoming and the discussion is excluded.

items.title: Campus dining trial
items.passage:
During the next two weeks, the dining hall will offer a smaller default portion with free second servings. This is intended to reduce food left on plates, not to limit how much students eat. Anyone can request the usual larger portion at the counter. We will weigh discarded food each evening and compare it with similar weekdays before the trial.
The comparison cannot isolate portion size perfectly: menu changes and attendance may also affect waste. Please complete the feedback card if the arrangement causes problems, particularly if you cannot easily return to the counter for another serving. Staff can bring an additional serving to your table on request. The trial applies only to the dining hall, not to packaged takeaway meals. We will publish the results before deciding whether to keep the system.

questions.stem: What is the trial intended to achieve?
options: Reduce plate waste while preserving access to more food
Restrict the amount each student may eat
Reduce takeaway package sizes
Replace student feedback with food weighing
questions.evidence: reduce food left on plates, not to limit how much students eat
questions.explanation: Evidence: “reduce food left on plates, not to limit how much students eat” Second servings and larger portions remain available.

questions.stem: Why are menu changes mentioned?
options: They could affect the comparison of waste totals
They prevent students from requesting more food
They require all portions to be identical
They explain why takeaway meals are included
questions.evidence: menu changes and attendance may also affect waste
questions.explanation: Evidence: “menu changes and attendance may also affect waste” The passage acknowledges other influences on the measured outcome.

options: Staff can bring another serving
They must buy a takeaway meal
They can obtain a refund only
They must leave the trial permanently
questions.evidence: bring an additional serving to your table on request
questions.explanation: Evidence: “bring an additional serving to your table on request” The accommodation addresses access to second servings.

items.title: Heritage building consultation
items.passage:
The council is considering converting the old station building into a community workspace. The exterior would be preserved, while interior partitions might be changed to provide accessible meeting rooms. No final design has been selected. We invite comments on how the space could serve residents, rather than applications to rent a particular room.
A preliminary plan is on display in the public library. It illustrates one possible layout and should not be read as an approved construction drawing. Written comments can be submitted until 20 June. An open meeting on 12 June will allow discussion, but attendance is not required to contribute. The council will summarize the themes raised and explain how they informed the next design stage. Funding has been requested; its availability will determine whether the project can proceed this year.

options: Ideas about community use of the space
Applications for particular rooms
Approved construction drawings
Offers to remove the exterior
questions.evidence: comments on how the space could serve residents

It has already authorized construction
It guarantees funding this year
It is the only layout residents may discuss
questions.evidence: one possible layout

Yes, before submitting any ideas
Only if they do not use the library
Only if funding has been approved
questions.evidence: attendance is not required to contribute
questions.explanation: Evidence: “attendance is not required to contribute” The meeting and written-comment route are alternatives.

items.title: Student publication invitation
items.passage:
The student magazine is accepting pieces about learning outside the classroom. We welcome essays, interviews, or illustrated reports, but not advertisements for paid services. A submission should describe an experience and reflect on what it taught the writer, rather than simply list activities.
The word limit is 800, excluding captions. Please include permission for any identifiable person's photograph. An interview subject's agreement to answer questions does not automatically grant permission to use their image. Editors may suggest cuts or ask for clarification before accepting a piece. Submission does not guarantee publication, and contributors will see the edited version before it goes to print. We cannot pay for contributions, but published writers receive two copies of the issue. The deadline is Friday at 6 p.m.; late pieces may be considered for a later issue rather than the current one.

questions.stem: What should a submission emphasize?
options: What the experience taught its writer
A list of paid services
The number of activities completed without reflection
An advertisement illustrated by an interview
questions.evidence: reflect on what it taught the writer

Consent to count captions in the word limit
Approval to receive payment for the interview
Permission to skip the edited-version review
questions.evidence: does not automatically grant permission to use their image

Every contributor receives payment
The word limit automatically rises
Late pieces are included in the current issue
questions.evidence: contributors will see the edited version
questions.explanation: Evidence: “contributors will see the edited version” Editorial changes are reviewed before publication.

items.title: Neighbourhood dog-walking service
items.passage:
I am offering lunchtime dog walks on weekdays within the north neighbourhood. Walks last forty minutes, with no more than two dogs together. Before accepting a regular booking, I meet the owner and dog for a short trial walk. This meeting is free and helps establish whether group walking is suitable.
Dogs that need individual walks can be considered, but the rate is higher because they occupy a full slot. I cannot provide overnight care or administer medication. If your usual lunchtime changes, let me know the previous evening; same-day changes are possible only if the route allows them. In severe weather I may shorten outdoor time and spend the remainder with the dog indoors, with the owner's agreement. The service area is limited so travel between clients does not reduce the time spent caring for each dog.

To charge for an additional full walking slot
To offer overnight care before booking
To replace all regular walks with group sessions

questions.stem: Why are individual walks more expensive?

They always last longer than forty minutes
They include overnight care
They require owners to administer medication
questions.evidence: because they occupy a full slot

At the start of the walk
After the week’s walks finish
Only during severe weather
questions.evidence: let me know the previous evening
questions.explanation: Evidence: “let me know the previous evening” Same-day changes are conditional on the route.

items.title: Student emergency grant
items.passage:
The student-support office has a small fund for unexpected essential expenses. It is not a scholarship for planned tuition costs. Applicants should explain the expense, why it was unforeseen, and what other help they have sought. A lack of receipts does not automatically prevent an application, but staff may request another way to verify the situation.
Decisions usually take five working days. If the need is immediate, contact the office before applying so staff can discuss temporary options; marking a form 'urgent' does not move it automatically to the front. Grants are based on assessed need and the remaining budget. Meeting the criteria does not guarantee the full amount requested. Information is reviewed privately by the support team and is not shared with teaching staff unless the applicant gives permission or a legal requirement applies.

All planned tuition payments
Awards based on academic ranking
Any expense without assessment

Write urgent and expect automatic priority
Wait for teaching staff to approve the form
Assume a full grant if the criteria are met

Seeking a scholarship for planned tuition
Requesting support without an essential expense
Treating the fund as an academic prize

items.title: Audio walking-guide trial
items.passage:
The town's new audio walking guide can be downloaded before you leave home. Once downloaded, it works without a network connection, except for the live opening-hours page. Those hours may change, so check them shortly before visiting a business. The narration describes buildings visible from public streets and does not authorize entry to private property.
The route can be completed in either direction. Numbered stops help users match audio tracks to places; they do not prescribe an order. We suggest allowing ninety minutes if you listen to every track, but you can skip stops and return later. Please use headphones at a volume that lets you hear traffic. During this trial, feedback about confusing directions is especially useful. Reviews of the restaurants themselves should be sent to the businesses, since the guide team does not manage them.

Downloaded narration
The numbered stop tracks
Instructions for either route direction
questions.evidence: except for the live opening-hours page

Yes, because the route works in one direction only
Only if they intend to skip a stop
Only when downloading at home
questions.evidence: they do not prescribe an order

Requests to enter private buildings
Reviews of the live network provider

items.title: Poster printing handoff
items.passage:

Mira 09:05: I have the poster ready, but the figures still show last month's numbers. Please don't send it to print yet.

Mira 09:10: Yes, and leave the editable file in our folder too.
Leah 11:45: The figures are updated. Owen had to leave, so I exported the PDF.

Mira 11:50: I'll check it now, then send the print order.

options: Leah
Owen
Mira

items.title: The value of negative results
items.passage:
A scientific experiment does not become informative only when it confirms a prediction. Suppose researchers test whether a coating makes a material more durable. If coated and uncoated samples perform similarly, the result can limit claims about the coating. It does not necessarily prove that the coating could never work: the test may cover only one temperature or one kind of wear.
Negative results are difficult to interpret when the procedure itself is uncertain. An insensitive measuring instrument might fail to detect a small improvement. Researchers therefore need to report how samples were selected, what was measured, and how precise the measurements were. These details help others distinguish evidence of little effect from a study unable to identify an effect.
Publication practices can also shape knowledge. If journals publish mainly positive findings, a reader may see an apparently consistent pattern while missing unsuccessful tests. Recording well-designed negative studies gives later researchers a more complete basis for deciding which explanations deserve further attention.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly arguing?
options: Well-documented negative results can contribute to scientific understanding
Careful instrument design is the main way to reduce the publication of unsuccessful experiments
Negative findings are chiefly useful for deciding which coating should be marketed
A failed coating test establishes the general durability of the uncoated material
questions.evidence: Recording well-designed negative studies
questions.explanation: Evidence: “Recording well-designed negative studies” The value depends on design and reporting, rather than on whether a prediction is confirmed.

questions.stem: Why might a study miss a small improvement?
options: Its measuring instrument may be insufficiently sensitive
Its samples were coated
Its findings were published
Its researchers described the temperature
questions.evidence: An insensitive measuring instrument might fail to detect a small improvement
questions.explanation: Evidence: “An insensitive measuring instrument might fail to detect a small improvement” Measurement sensitivity is the stated limitation.

questions.stem: What can an unsuccessful test at one temperature establish?
options: A limit on claims under the tested conditions
That the coating fails under every temperature
That uncoated materials cannot be durable
That publication practices have no influence
questions.evidence: the test may cover only one temperature
questions.explanation: Evidence: “the test may cover only one temperature” The evidence applies to a limited setting and cannot support universal failure.

questions.stem: What does “These details” refer to?
options: Information about sampling, measurement, and precision
The coating’s advertising claims
Only the number of journal readers
The positive findings of other researchers
questions.evidence: how samples were selected, what was measured, and how precise the measurements were
questions.explanation: Evidence: “how samples were selected, what was measured, and how precise the measurements were” The phrase points to the reporting information in the preceding sentence.

questions.stem: Why discuss journals’ preference for positive findings?
options: To explain how the available record can become incomplete
To argue that all positive results are fabricated
To recommend abandoning material tests
To show that temperature controls publication
questions.evidence: missing unsuccessful tests
questions.explanation: Evidence: “missing unsuccessful tests” Selective publication can make an apparent pattern stronger than the full evidence warrants.

items.title: How a shoreline records change
items.passage:
A shoreline drawn on a map may appear to be a fixed boundary, but the water's edge moves with tides, weather, and sediment transport. Comparing two maps can therefore suggest a change that partly reflects different conditions at the time of observation. A careful comparison uses a consistent definition of the shoreline and records when each measurement was made.
Sediment does not simply move from land toward the sea. Waves approaching at an angle can carry sand along a coast, redistributing it between neighbouring beaches. A structure that traps sand in one place may leave less available farther along the shore. The benefit at a protected beach must therefore be considered alongside changes elsewhere.
Long observation periods are especially useful because a storm may remove sand that later returns during calmer conditions. A measurement made immediately after the storm could exaggerate a lasting loss. Researchers combine repeated surveys with information about waves and tides to distinguish short-term variation from a persistent trend.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: Shoreline change must be interpreted using consistent and repeated observations
Storm erosion is the principal cause of lasting shoreline retreat
Coastal protection is most effective when sand is trapped near a single beach
Using the newest map removes the need to compare observation conditions
questions.evidence: distinguish short-term variation from a persistent trend
questions.explanation: Evidence: “distinguish short-term variation from a persistent trend” The passage explains why definitions, conditions, and time span matter.

questions.stem: How can waves redistribute sand between beaches?
options: By carrying it along the coast
By removing only the largest grains
By fixing the water’s edge permanently
By reducing all tidal movement
questions.evidence: carry sand along a coast
questions.explanation: Evidence: “carry sand along a coast” Angled waves support movement alongshore, not only offshore.

questions.stem: What might happen beyond a structure that traps sand?
options: Another beach may receive less sediment
Every beach will become wider
Tides will cease to affect mapping
The structure will eliminate future storms
questions.evidence: leave less available farther along the shore
questions.explanation: Evidence: “leave less available farther along the shore” Local sediment capture can affect supply to neighbouring areas.

questions.stem: What does “persistent” mean in the final sentence?
options: Continuing over time
Immediately visible
Measured without tides
Occurring only once
questions.evidence: a persistent trend
questions.explanation: Evidence: “a persistent trend” It contrasts with short-term variation rather than with visible change.

questions.stem: Why mention sand returning after a storm?
options: To illustrate how a temporary loss can be mistaken for a lasting one
To prove that storms never change coasts
To recommend surveying only in calm weather
To explain why maps use different colours
questions.evidence: sand that later returns during calmer conditions
questions.explanation: Evidence: “sand that later returns during calmer conditions” A single post-storm measurement can misrepresent longer-term change.

items.title: The work of a dictionary
items.passage:
Dictionaries are sometimes treated as authorities that decide which words people may use. In practice, many dictionaries describe usage by examining evidence from speech and writing. Editors gather examples, identify recurring meanings, and decide whether a new use is sufficiently established to include. Entry does not imply that every speaker approves of the word.
The evidence available to editors is uneven. Published texts are easier to collect than informal conversations, and some communities produce more searchable writing than others. A word may therefore be common in daily speech before it appears frequently in a written collection. Editors can address this imbalance by drawing on different kinds of material, although no collection represents every speaker equally.
Definitions also require judgment. A familiar word can develop a new meaning gradually, making it difficult to decide where one sense ends and another begins. Examples help readers see how a word operates in context. The dictionary is thus a carefully organized account of language evidence, rather than a complete inventory of all possible expression.

questions.stem: How does the author characterize dictionaries?
options: As organized interpretations of evidence about language use
Dictionary inclusion gives a word an approved meaning that speakers should follow
Published language is more representative than informal speech because it is easier to collect
Changes in word meaning are resolved by choosing the most familiar definition
questions.evidence: a carefully organized account of language evidence
questions.explanation: Evidence: “a carefully organized account of language evidence” Editors use evidence and judgment; neither arbitrary rules nor complete coverage describes the process.

questions.stem: Why may spoken words be underrepresented?
options: Informal conversation is harder to collect than published text
Speech contains fewer meanings than writing
Editors refuse to examine spoken material
Every community writes equally often
